questions.q: Why does the terraform apply output in this lesson contain no surprises?
options: Because no resources were actually created
Because Terraform always succeeds regardless of configuration
Because the apply was run without reviewing anything first
Because the prior terraform plan already showed exactly what would be created
questions.explain: Since the plan was reviewed and matched expectations in the previous lesson, the apply output matches it exactly with 12 resources added.

questions.q: What does terraform destroy use to know exactly what to remove and in what order?
options: The same state file used to build the environment, removed in reverse dependency order
A manual list typed in by the user
The cloud provider's billing records
A separate destroy.tf file
questions.explain: terraform destroy reads the existing state file to determine every managed resource and removes them in the reverse of the order they were created.

questions.q: According to the lesson, why should a dev-only capstone environment be destroyed rather than left running?
options: Terraform requires environments to be destroyed within 24 hours
Because providers block long-running dev environments
To avoid ongoing cloud costs and to prove the configuration can rebuild the environment from nothing
Because state files expire automatically
questions.explain: A scratch or dev environment used only to prove a pattern works should be torn down to avoid unnecessary cost, and destroying it also proves the configuration is reproducible from scratch.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend leading with when presenting this capstone in a portfolio or interview?
options: The specific decisions and tradeoffs behind the project, such as why directory-per-environment was chosen over workspaces
The exact dollar cost of the cloud resources created
A list of every HCL keyword used
Simply stating that Terraform was used
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes explaining the reasoning behind design choices — not just naming the tool used — as the stronger way to present the project.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about what's next after completing this course?
options: The DevOps Engineer path is now fully complete with no further courses
There is no further guidance given
The student is ready for what's next in the DevOps Engineer path, having built an end-to-end understanding of Terraform across both Azure and AWS
The student must now repeat this course from the beginning
questions.explain: The lesson closes by congratulating the student on completing this course and noting they're ready to continue with the next course in the DevOps Engineer path.
